narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses for approval, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in that decision. First, the length of the loan you requested had the strongest influence overall. At only 10 months it was considerably shorter than the 19-month average among approved applicants; while this shorter term actually pulled the prediction slightly toward approval, the model still saw the overall picture as too risky. 

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account. You currently have between 0 and 200 DM in it. This is less common among people who are approved (only 18% of approved applicants show this balance range), and it pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk.

Third, the total amount you asked to borrow also mattered. At 1,521 DM this was about half the average request from approved applicants. This lower amount worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval, yet it was not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your checking-account status and the combination of other details in your file.

Because your checking-account balance was the main negative driver, the clearest next step is to build a stronger positive balance over the coming months, then reapply. This single change often improves outcomes substantially.
